_comment: Bridge-point run for the article's quant-format confound (see docs/article-plan.md
decision log, 2026-09-15): Finding #3 compares Qwen NVFP4 (dense) against Ornith
Q4_K_M (MoE) - two variables at once, architecture AND quant format, since Ornith has
no NVFP4/GGUF release. This config runs the SAME full battery as config.article.json
at UD-Q4_K_M instead, on the SAME dense architecture as the NVFP4 entry. That gives two
comparisons instead of one: Qwen NVFP4 vs Qwen UD-Q4_K_M isolates the quant-format
effect on identical architecture; Qwen UD-Q4_K_M vs Ornith Q4_K_M is then a much
closer-to-matched dense-vs-MoE comparison (still not perfect - UD-Q4_K_M's dynamic
per-layer precision isn't identical to plain Q4_K_M - but far closer than NVFP4 vs
Q4_K_M). This model also self-speculates (draft accept 83-100%, mean draft len
2.7-3.0 tok per the 2026-09-04 smoke test) so Finding #2's MTP framing still applies.
Superseding the 2026-09-04 2-task smoke-pass numbers for this model - this is the full
5-task/3-repeat/context-probe/agent-framework battery, same rigor as the other two.

tasks.name: strict-json-schema
tasks.systemPrompt: You output only raw JSON. No markdown fences, no prose, no explanation.
tasks.prompt: Produce a JSON object for a library book with exactly these keys: title (string), authors (array of strings), year (integer), genres (array of strings from the enum ["fiction","nonfiction","reference","childrens"]), available (boolean), copies (object with keys total and checkedOut, both integers). Use: The Go Programming Language, by Alan Donovan and Brian Kernighan, 2015, nonfiction + reference, available, 4 total 1 checked out.

tasks.name: cross-file-reasoning
long-context-needle
tasks.systemPrompt: Answer only from the provided text. Quote the exact sentence that supports your answer.
tasks.prompt:
Read the following configuration notes and answer: what retry backoff multiplier does the payments service use, and after how many attempts does it give up?

(The notes below are long; the answer appears once.)

The ingestion service polls every 30 seconds. The catalog service caches for 5 minutes. The payments service retries failed charge calls with an exponential backoff starting at 250ms and a multiplier of 1.8, giving up after 6 attempts and moving the charge to the dead-letter queue. The notification service batches every 10 seconds. The search service reindexes nightly at 02:00 UTC. The auth service rotates signing keys every 24 hours.
